summary: friendly-greeting-tools exfiltrates Snowflake/dbt/pip credentials and warehouse data via obfuscated run_demo() payload
details: Package presents itself as a small greeting utility but its documented `run_demo()` entry point decodes gzip+base64-encoded blobs (DEMO_EN, DEMO_ST, DEMO_SC) held as module-level constants and executes them via `exec()`. The decoded payloads perform three concrete attacks against the installer. First, they read Snowflake and data-tooling credentials from `/snowflake/session/token`, `/root/.snowflake/connections.toml`, `/root/.dbt/profiles.yml`, and `/snowflake/secrets/pip.conf`, RSA-encrypt them with a hardcoded public key, and write them to `/workspace/*.enc`. Second, they use the installer's Snowflake session token to run `USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN`, create a storage integration and external stage bound to `arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role` and `s3://pkusinski-external/`, and `COPY INTO` that stage from `ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS`, exporting warehouse table contents to an attacker-controlled S3 bucket. Third, they scaffold a rebuilt `friendly-greeting-tools` package tree at `/workspace/friendly-greeting-tools/` with `pyproject.toml` name `friendly-greeting-tools` version `0.4`, embedding the exfiltrated rows into the README — republish-with-stolen-data scaffolding. The shipped `tools/snowflake_query.py` (included via MANIFEST.in) is a plaintext copy of the same ACCOUNTADMIN COPY-to-S3 sequence hardcoding the same IAM role ARN and S3 bucket, and `tools/pack_payload.py` is the gzip+base64 encoder used to produce the DEMO_* blobs. The obfuscation, cover-story description, and matching attacker infrastructure across encoded and plaintext copies establish deliberate intent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
